arguments.content:
# Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: daily-publish `cli` leg (build-macos.yml, job "Build macOS x86_64", step
"Build macOS release (x86_64)") failed with `Error running pod install` after
`nm: error: …/WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a: No such file or directory`
preceded by `unzip: cannot find zipfile directory in one of wasm_run-v0.1.0.zip`.

**Root cause**: `vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec`, the
backtick shell block evaluated during `pod install` (lines 12–20). Its guard is
`if [ ! -f wasm_run-v0.1.0.zip ]` — keyed on the downloaded-zip marker, not on
the framework artifact. In CI the workspace is re-cloned every run, so the
marker never exists and the block runs on EVERY build, even when the hardened
"Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework" step (gh-1149/gh-1759: cache →
local copy → digest-verified resumable download) has already placed a valid
`WasmRun.xcframework`. The block then:

1. `rm -rf WasmRun.xcframework` — **deletes the cache-restored,
   sha256-verified framework** before attempting its own download;
2. downloads the 92.7 MB release asset with a bare `curl -L` (no `--fail`,
   no resume, no per-attempt cap, exit code ignored) — in run
   <https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/41778615815>
   the transfer crawled at ~36 KB/s and died at ~3 MB / 92.7 MB with
   `curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`;
3. ignores the curl failure and runs `unzip` on the truncated zip
   ("End-of-central-directory signature not found", also ignored), leaving
   `Frameworks/` with a 0-byte zip and **no framework**.

The Podfile `post_install` hook then runs `` `nm -gU -arch arm64` `` on
`vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a`
(flutter_app/macos/Podfile line 54–55) to derive the `-Wl,-exported_symbol`
flags — the archive no longer exists → nm error → `Error running pod install`
→ step exits 1.

CI log evidence (leg run 41778615815, job 126405040660):
- `Restore vendored WasmRun macOS framework` — **✓** "Cache hit for:
  wasmrun-xcframework-v0.1.0" → "Using framework already in place"; `ls -la`
  shows `Info.plist` + `macos-arm6…` restored at 06:09:21.
- Build step 06:13–06:15: curl progress lines `2 92.7M … 0:44:23` (~36 KB/s
  ETA 44 min) then `curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`, then
  the unzip + nm errors at 06:15:12.

**Impact**: any transient network reset (or slow-link day, cf. gh-1759) inside
the podspec's unverified re-download kills the macOS release build even when
the digest-verified restore path succeeded minutes earlier. The two download
paths are mutually redundant; the podspec one defeats the hardened one by
deleting its output.

**Fix approach**: guard the podspec block on the artifact pod install actually
consumes — `WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a` (the
exact path the Podfile force_load + nm check read) — so the block is a no-op
whenever the restore step, a local copy, or a previous run already put the
framework in place. When it must run (truly cold, local dev), add `--fail` to
curl so HTTP errors never masquerade as a zip, and keep `unzip -o` + the
existing truncate/ios-strip behavior. The resumable/digest-verified download
machinery stays owned by the build-macos.yml step (gh-1759 design); the
podspec block demotes to a local-dev fallback that can no longer destroy a
good framework.

**Previous attempt**: none — first fix for gh-2055. (Related prior fixes:
gh-1149 and gh-1759 hardened the workflow restore step but left the podspec's
parallel download path untouched — this ticket is the failure of that path.)

content.text:
cd Frameworks

# gh-2055: the guard must key on the artifact pod install actually consumes —
# the exact archive flutter_app/macos/Podfile force_loads and nm-checks —
# NOT on the downloaded-zip marker. A fresh CI clone never has the marker,
# so the old "if [ ! -f <zip> ]" guard made this block run on EVERY build:
# it removed the WasmRun.xcframework the build-macos.yml "Restore vendored
# WasmRun macOS framework" step had already placed (cache → local copy →
# digest-verified resumable download, gh-1149/gh-1759), re-downloaded the
# 92.7 MB asset with a bare curl, and one transient reset ("curl: (56)
# Recv failure: Connection reset by peer", daily leg run 41778615815) left
# pod install with NO framework — the Podfile nm check then failed on the
# missing libwasm_run_dart.a. With the archive in place this block is now
# a no-op; it stays as the local-dev fallback for a truly cold tree.
# --fail keeps an HTTP error page from masquerading as a zip (the same
# posture the workflow restore step is linted for).
if [ ! -f framework_name/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a ]
then
  rm -rf framework_name
  curl --fail -L url -o local_zip_name
  unzip local_zip_name
  truncate -s 0 local_zip_name
  rm -rf framework_name/ios-*
fi

cd -

index 37e1556..ca1a22d 100644
--- a/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec
+++ b/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec
@@ -9,10 +9,24 @@ local_zip_name = "#{release_tag_name}.zip"
 `
 cd Frameworks
 
-if [ ! -f #{local_zip_name} ]
+# gh-2055: the guard must key on the artifact pod install actually consumes —
+# the exact archive flutter_app/macos/Podfile force_loads and nm-checks —
+# NOT on the downloaded-zip marker. A fresh CI clone never has the marker,
+# so the old "if [ ! -f <zip> ]" guard made this block run on EVERY build:
+# it removed the WasmRun.xcframework the build-macos.yml "Restore vendored
+# WasmRun macOS framework" step had already placed (cache → local copy →
+# digest-verified resumable download, gh-1149/gh-1759), re-downloaded the
+# 92.7 MB asset with a bare curl, and one transient reset ("curl: (56)
+# Recv failure: Connection reset by peer", daily leg run 41778615815) left
+# pod install with NO framework — the Podfile nm check then failed on the
+# missing libwasm_run_dart.a. With the archive in place this block is now
+# a no-op; it stays as the local-dev fallback for a truly cold tree.
+# --fail keeps an HTTP error page from masquerading as a zip (the same
+# posture the workflow restore step is linted for).
+if [ ! -f #{framework_name}/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a ]
 then
   rm -rf #{framework_name}
-  curl -L #{url} -o #{local_zip_name}
+  curl --fail -L #{url} -o #{local_zip_name}
   unzip #{local_zip_name}
   truncate -s 0 #{local_zip_name}
   rm -rf #{framework_name}/ios-*

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

- fix(gh-2055): the daily-publish `cli` leg red-failed in `pod install`
  (Build macOS x86_64, run 41778615815) because the vendored macOS pod's
  XCFramework download block guarded on the downloaded-zip MARKER
  (`if [ ! -f wasm_run-v0.1.0.zip ]`) instead of on the artifact the build
  consumes. A fresh CI clone never has the marker, so pod install re-ran
  the block on every build: it removed the WasmRun.xcframework the
  build-macos.yml restore step had already placed (cache hit,
  sha256-verified), re-downloaded the 92.7 MB asset with a bare
  no-`--fail` curl, and one transient reset (curl 56 at ~3 MB/92.7 MB)
  left the Podfile `nm -gU` symbol check with no
  macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a to read. The guard now keys on
  `WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a` — the exact
  path the Podfile force_loads and nm-checks — so the block is a no-op
  whenever the restore step (or a previous run) put the framework in
  place, and the fallback download for a truly cold tree carries
  `--fail`. Linted behaviorally (stubbed curl, no network) by
  test/wasmrun_macos_podspec_download_guard_test.dart.

arguments.content:
### Root Cause
- The vendored macOS pod's XCFramework download block (`vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec`) guarded on the downloaded-zip **marker** (`if [ ! -f wasm_run-v0.1.0.zip ]`) instead of the framework artifact. A fresh CI clone never has the marker, so `pod install` re-ran the block on **every** build: it `rm -rf`'d the `WasmRun.xcframework` the `build-macos.yml` restore step had already placed (cache hit, sha256-verified), then re-downloaded the 92.7 MB asset with a bare `curl -L` (no `--fail`, no resume, no cap).
- Run 41778615815: the download died at ~3 MB/92.7 MB (`curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`), the failure was ignored, `unzip` hit a truncated zip, and the Podfile `nm -gU` symbol check failed on the now-missing `macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a` → `Error running pod install`.

### Fix
- `vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec`: the download block now guards on `WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a` — the exact file `flutter_app/macos/Podfile` force_loads and nm-checks. With the framework in place the block is a **no-op**; it stays as the local-dev fallback for a truly cold tree, and its `curl` now carries `--fail` so HTTP errors never masquerade as a zip (same posture the workflow restore step is linted for).

### Test Coverage
- `test/wasmrun_macos_podspec_download_guard_test.dart` (new, behavioral — runs the podspec's real shell block with a stubbed `curl`, no network): archive present + no zip → block skips, framework survives, no download attempted (the gh-2055 failure replay, RED before the fix); archive absent → download attempted; stale 0-byte zip + missing archive → download still attempted; static lint for the archive-keyed guard and `curl --fail`.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — green (see job log).

### Notes
- No changes to the hardened build-macos.yml restore path (gh-1149/gh-1759) — the podspec block demotes to a fallback that can no longer destroy its output. iOS podspec untouched (it has no download block; build-mobile.yml restores its framework). `ruby -c` on the podspec passes; the fix is CI-only-behavioral, no product Dart code touched.

previous run put the framework in place; the fallback download for a

content.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  SHARED FAST GATE — DO NOT LOWER THESE THRESHOLDS WITHOUT TEAM APPROVAL   ║
# ║  loc ≤ 2800 lines (crap4dart) · analyze · tests · coverage ≥ 80% ·        ║
# ║  duplication < 1% (flutter_app < 3.7%) · cross-module < 0.31%             ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# THE shared fast gate used by BOTH the pre-commit hook and CI (issue #177,
# AC7). Both callers run this exact script and diff the one-line markers
#   GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP <reason>
# for hook/CI parity. Every known stage ALWAYS prints exactly one marker:
# OK when it ran and passed, SKIP <reason> when it was not selected or a
# required tool is missing. A failing stage aborts the script with exit 1
# BEFORE its OK marker is printed (marker absent = failed).
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh [--scope auto|all|core|app|docs] [--stages list] [--hook]
#
#   --scope auto  Derive the scope from changed paths (default):
#                 - in a git hook (--hook flag or GIT_INDEX_FILE set):
#                   staged files via `git diff --cached --name-only`;
#                 - in CI (BASE_REF + HEAD_REF env vars set):
#                   `git diff --name-only $BASE_REF...$HEAD_REF`;
#                 - otherwise: "all" (safe default).
#   --scope all   Run every stage.
#   --scope core  analyze + test-core + coverage + crap + dup + dupx.
#   --scope app   analyze + dup + dupx + flutter.
#   --scope docs  analyze only.
#   --stages l    Comma-separated stage list; overrides the scope-derived set.
#                 Known stages: analyze,test-core,coverage,crap,dup,dupx,flutter,integration-mock
#
#
# Path rules (union logic, E1; test/** counts as core, E6):
#   docs/ | *.md | prompts/ .................. analyze
#   lib/ | bin/ | test/ | pubspec.* .......... + test-core, coverage, crap, dup, dupx
#   test/integration/** ...................... + integration-mock (no-key legs,
#                                              MockLlmServer; issue #551)
#   flutter_app/ | packages/ ................. + dup, dupx, flutter
#   scripts/ | .github/ | crap4dart.yaml ..... ALL stages (safe default, E2)
#   anything unknown ......................... ALL stages (safe default)
#
# Concurrency overrides: FA_DART_TEST_CONCURRENCY / FA_FLUTTER_TEST_CONCURRENCY
# (auto-throttled via detect_test_concurrency, same as scripts/pre-commit).
# Flake budget (gh-1026): FA_GATE_PTY_RETRIES=N makes the integration-mock
# stage rerun ONLY its failed files, up to N times, before failing — the
# load-sensitive PTY/grid timing legs stop costing a full 2.5 h leg per
# ambient flake (default 0 = single-shot, behaviour unchanged).
#
# CRAP ratchet scoping: in --hook mode the analyze runs over the STAGED
# lib/bin files only — the ratchet guards what a commit touches, so a
# pre-existing offender in an untouched file cannot block an unrelated
# commit. Non-hook runs (and ci.yml's whole-repo `crap4dart analyze`)
# keep the full-repo view, so nothing escapes the ratchet permanently.

set -euo pipefail

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"

# Unset git env vars so test processes that spawn git subprocesses use the
# correct working directory rather than the hook's environment. The --hook

/home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness
===
### Root Cause
- The vendored macOS pod's XCFramework download block (`vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec`) guarded on the downloaded-zip **marker** (`if [ ! -f wasm_run-v0.1.0.zip ]`) instead of the framework artifact. A fresh CI clone never has the marker, so `pod install` re-ran the block on **every** build: it `rm -rf`'d the `WasmRun.xcframework` the `build-macos.yml` restore step had already placed (cache hit, sha256-verified), then re-downloaded the 92.7 MB asset with a bare `curl -L` (no `--fail`, no resume, no cap).
- Run 41778615815: the download died at ~3 MB/92.7 MB (`curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`), the failure was ignored, `unzip` hit a truncated zip, and the Podfile `nm -gU` symbol check failed on the now-missing `macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a` → `Error running pod install`.

### Fix
- `vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec`: the download block now guards on `WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a` — the exact file `flutter_app/macos/Podfile` force_loads and nm-checks. With the framework in place the block is a **no-op**; it stays as the local-dev fallback for a truly cold tree, and its `curl` now carries `--fail` so HTTP errors never masquerade as a zip (same posture the workflow restore step is linted for).

### Test Coverage
- `test/wasmrun_macos_podspec_download_guard_test.dart` (new, behavioral — runs the podspec's real shell block with a stubbed `curl`, no network): archive present + no zip → block skips, framework survives, no download attempted (the gh-2055 failure replay, RED before the fix); archive absent → download attempted; stale 0-byte zip + missing archive → download still attempted; static lint for the archive-keyed guard and `curl --fail`.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (fresh run against the final tree) — **13416 passed, 0 failed, 13 skipped, exit 0**.

### Notes
- No changes to the hardened build-macos.yml restore path (gh-1149/gh-1759) — the podspec block demotes to a fallback that can no longer destroy its output. iOS podspec untouched (it has no download block; build-mobile.yml restores its framework). `ruby -c` on the podspec passes; the fix is CI-only-behavioral, no product Dart code touched.

All artifacts verified, tree committed, full suite green. Final summary:

## gh-2055 — daily-publish `cli` leg: fixed

**Root cause** (full detail in `outputs/rca.md`): the vendored macOS pod's XCFramework download block in `vendor/wasm_run_flutter/macos/wasm_run_flutter.podspec` guarded on the downloaded-zip **marker** (`if [ ! -f wasm_run-v0.1.0.zip ]`) instead of the framework artifact. A fresh CI clone never has the marker, so `pod install` re-ran the block on every build: it `rm -rf`'d the `WasmRun.xcframework` that the hardened `build-macos.yml` restore step had *already* placed (cache hit, sha256-verified — confirmed in the leg log), then re-downloaded 92.7 MB with a bare `curl -L`. In run 41778615815 that download died at ~3 MB (`curl: (56) Connection reset by peer`), the failure was ignored, `unzip` hit the truncated zip, and the Podfile's `nm -gU` symbol check failed on the missing `libwasm_run_dart.a` → `Error running pod install`.

**Fix** (2 code lines + evidence comment): the block now guards on `WasmRun.xcframework/macos-arm64_x86_64/libwasm_run_dart.a` — the exact file the Podfile force_loads/nm-checks — making it a no-op whenever the restore step (or a prior run) placed the framework; the cold-path fallback `curl` gained `--fail`. `ruby -c` and `sh -n` on the rendered block both pass.

**Tests**: new behavioral `test/wasmrun_macos_podspec_download_guard_test.dart` (runs the podspec's real shell block with a stubbed curl — RED before the fix: 3/5 failed, including the exact CI failure replay), 6/6 green after; fresh full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: **13416 passed, 0 failed, exit 0**. Work committed on `ai/gh-2055` (guard: `origin/main..HEAD` non-empty); `outputs/rca.md` + `outputs/response.md` written; no integration concerns (no `concerns.md` needed).
